did_you_know.text: Did you know? This verse mentions both “my messenger,” who prepares the way, and “the messenger of the covenant,” whose coming the people await; the Lord will suddenly come to his temple.
Did you know? The day of the Lord’s coming is described through two images of purification: a refiner’s fire and cleansing soap.
Did you know? The purification process is directed especially toward the sons of Levi, so that they may be refined and offer sacrifices to the Lord in righteousness.

Did you know? The list of sins in this verse includes sorcery, adultery, perjury, exploiting hired workers, and mistreating widows, orphans, and foreigners; this emphasizes that divine judgment also concerns social and moral relationships.

Did you know? The people are commanded to bring the entire tithe to the storehouse, and the verse describes the blessing as the opening of heaven’s floodgates and the pouring out of blessings beyond measure.

Did you know? When those who fear the Lord speak with one another, the Lord is described as listening and hearing, and a book of remembrance is written before him for those who fear the Lord and honor his name.
Did you know? The day of the Lord is described as burning like a furnace, with the wicked and evildoers compared to stubble that is burned up; the verse emphasizes that no root or branch will remain.
Did you know? Near the end of the book, there is a call to remember the law of Moses, which he was commanded at Horeb to give to all Israel, including its statutes and ordinances.
Did you know? Before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord, the Lord promises to send the prophet Elijah.

Did you know? Elijah’s role is described as turning the hearts of the fathers to their children and the hearts of the children to their fathers; the verse presents this as a way to prevent the land from being struck with a curse.
